quizName: Hardest Questions in Idaho Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It has white background with red and black markings. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What should be your first consideration when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.explanation: Protection is most important when buying a helmet. Choose a helmet that fits well, fastens securely, and meets DOT safety standards.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle while carrying a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride a little faster than you normally would.
Start slowing earlier than you normally would.
Merge into smaller gaps of traffic than you normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing earlier than you normally would.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. This extra weight makes your motorcycle respond more slowly. It takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. Start slowing down earlier when you have a passenger.

questions.question: You should always perform a head check before:
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles. Your mirrors cannot show everything. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, merging, or passing.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: Follow each other as closely as possible.
Not worry about distances between members.

questions.explanation: When riding in a group, use a staggered formation. This formation keeps riders close together while maintaining safe distances between each rider.

questions.question: What should you do if you must ride on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed. Avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes gently.

questions.question: You should pick a lane position that:

options.text: Best increases your visibility and allows for a safe cushion of space.
You like, without regard to others.
Gets you close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Best increases your visibility and allows for a safe cushion of space.
questions.explanation: Position yourself where other drivers can see you best. Keep space around your motorcycle for safety. Change your position as road conditions change. No single position is always best.

questions.question: Improper braking:

options.text: Is a significant contributing factor to many motorcycle crashes.
Should not be a concern, since the motorcycle has two brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a significant contributing factor to many motorcycle crashes.
questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Learning proper braking technique is important for safe riding.

questions.question: Taking over-the-counter medication before riding:

options.text: Is usually fine since over-the-counter medications are never very strong.
May affect your riding abilities and should be done with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: May affect your riding abilities and should be done with caution.
questions.explanation: Many medications, including over-the-counter drugs, have side effects that can impair your riding ability. Talk to your doctor about how any new medication may affect your driving or riding.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing to be more visible to other drivers. Reflective materials also help improve your visibility.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black symbols warn drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: You have a better chance of surviving a crash if you wear:
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets DOT standards gives the best head and neck protection. Wearing a good quality helmet that fits properly is the single best thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, focus most on the helmet's:
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important thing to think about when buying a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: A motorcycle must have all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Idaho requires motorcycles to have fenders on both wheels, a brake on at least one wheel, a headlight, a horn, a mirror, a muffler, a brake light, a taillight, and at least one rear reflector. If you carry passengers, you must also have a passenger seat and footrests.

questions.question: When you drink alcohol faster:

options.text: The faster it leaves your body.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: Drinking faster means alcohol builds up in your body quickly. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you have more than one drink per hour, alcohol will still be in your system after an hour.

questions.question: Reflective and brightly-colored helmets and clothing:

options.text: Should only be worn when riding at night.
Help make motorcycle riders more visible.
Do not increase motorcycle rider safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help make motorcycle riders more visible.
questions.explanation: Wearing brightly-colored or reflective clothing helps other drivers see you better on the road.

questions.question: Blind spots on motorcycles:

options.text: Should be checked regularly by riders.
Don't exist if the motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be checked regularly by riders.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spots before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your normal routine.

questions.question: Use your mirrors when stopping at an intersection to:

options.text: See if drivers behind you know you are stopping.
Look for dark clouds that may indicate bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: See if drivers behind you know you are stopping.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when stopping to make sure drivers behind you see you and are reacting to your stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, look for other traffic or pedestrians, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume that other drivers will yield to you.
Change your lane position to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position to be more visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the lane position where other drivers can see you best.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same location as on your motorcycle.
Take it out on the highway right away.
Learn how to use it in a safe, controlled area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn how to use it in a safe, controlled area first.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding a new motorcycle, learn where all the controls are. Practice riding it in a safe area before going on the road.

questions.question: When you travel at night, judging distances is:

options.text: About the same as during the day.

questions.explanation: It is harder to judge how far away objects are when driving at night. During the day, shadows and light help you see distance. At night, artificial lights may distort these visual clues or hide them completely.

questions.question: To get the most protection from your helmet, make sure it:
questions.explanation: Your helmet will protect you best if it meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards, fits snugly all around, and has no damage.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Only wear a jacket at night.
Only wear a jacket when it is cold.

questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding a motorcycle, no matter how warm the weather is.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:

options.text: Check that your brake lights work.
Check that the paint is not peeling.
Make sure the bike is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that your brake lights work.
questions.explanation: Do a safety check before every ride. Test your brakes to make sure each one turns on the brake lights.
